summary_paragraph: A female patient with systemic lupus erythematosus and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted with fevers, right upper quadrant abdominal pain, and shortness of breath. Imaging revealed a hypodense lesion in the upper pole of the right kidney with perinephric stranding, concerning for a renal or perinephric abscess. She was started on IV pip/tazo and vancomycin, with vancomycin administered slowly due to a history of Red Man syndrome. Blood cultures were negative. An abdominal ultrasound confirmed a focal hypoechoic lesion consistent with bacterial nephritis but no drainable collection. Her respiratory symptoms improved after hemodialysis, attributed to volume overload. She remained afebrile with stable pain controlled on hydromorphone. She was discharged on oral ciprofloxacin and IV vancomycin to be administered during outpatient hemodialysis for a 14-day course, with instructions to monitor for fever and obtain a follow-up ultrasound.
